items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: And then I went with Kid René's band. That was up until 1922.

ctx.x: I know a lot of people bought those and they wouldn't even have a part for them in late years anymore.

Yeah, late years they cut it. They changed the orchestration. Orchestration used to be put up for shell and oboe and all that stuff as time went to change. But anyway, we formed this band called Lawrence Murad and I. It was the original Diamond Band. And we had Bush Hall on the trumpet. That's the time I'd taken a wife. We weren't making much money. And then I went with Kid René's band. That was up until 1922. And I went with Kid René's band. I wanted to get me, especially Simon Murad was in the band. So I quit…

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: So when Rene heard me play, he was so enthused over my saxophone playing, he got me in the band.

ctx.x: Well they've got two styles. One fellow would play a style where he was making a lot of notes. My kid punched you. Oh yeah. Dadda dadda dadda. Yeah. All that.

You'd run all that too. And Buddy would run beautiful notes like that too. But Rene didn't use that. Rene punched out the melody and swang the melody. And swang the whole house too. Yeah? That's great. So when Rene heard me play, he was so enthused over my saxophone playing, he got me in the band. And that made it, he's there real great. Because there was a saxophone playing, and he was playing with me. And then afterwards they finally got saxophone. So finally a musician was an insurance collector and he told…

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: But Kid Rene, I used to play that number, with Kid Rene.

ctx.x: You said that, remember that number we recorded the other day, Sand Dunes? You said that was one of Buddy's numbers? Is that where you first heard that number? By Buddy playing it? Did I? That number we recorded the other day, Sand Dunes. I understand. Is that where you first heard that number, by Buddy Petit playing it, or did you?
I first heard it with Kid Rene. But I did hear Buddy play it too. But Kid Rene, I used to play that number, with Kid Rene. That was one of his main numbers.
You were saying yesterday, not yesterday, when we came by here last, you were explaining to us that Kid Rene used to play it differently to Buddy. Do you remember? That who?
